header:
Date: 2026-06-11
Time: 15:00 - 15:42 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Synergy CTO), Ethan Brooks (Lead SRE), Linh Tran (Platform Engineer)
Recording: Fireflies transcription
Shared files: Redwood integration deck (link shared in chat); sample benchmark spreadsheet referenced
summary: Discovery focused on integration options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), SDK support (LangChain/LlamaIndex), gateway/proxy patterns, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Customer cares about latency SLOs for edge regions, data residency, and SSO/KMS requirements. Agreed to follow up with SDK examples, pricing, and a technical deep-dive+benchmark run.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account. We also have Priya, our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Maya Patel: Hi Jordan, Priya. Thanks. I got the invite, eager to understand how we'd plug Redwood into our stack.
[00:15] Priya Shah: Hey Maya, Ethan, Linh. Quick agenda — integration options, SDKs and LangChain/LlamaIndex support, gateway and proxy patterns, rate limits/quota model, and observability hooks. Then open Q&A.
[00:28] Ethan Brooks: Sounds good. We're re-evaluating hosted endpoints vs dedicated pools because of latency spikes during peak billing cycles, so curious about routing and fallback.
[00:35] Maya Patel: Also SSO/SAML and our compliance needs — SOC2 and audit logs.
[00:40] Priya Shah: Totally. We'll cover security later. Quick question on traffic shape — average qps and token mix?
[00:50] Ethan Brooks: Right now our stg traffic is about 80 qps across two regions, peaks to 350 qps for short windows. Typical prompt length 40-90 tokens, but embeddings batch jobs are heavy at night.
[01:07] Priya Shah: That's helpful. For 80-350 qps, dedicated pools or burst to dedicated from hosted can make sense. Our Dedicated offering gives you reserved GPU capacity and predictable throughput; Hosted has autoscaling but with potential cold-start variability.
[01:28] Linh Tran: Do you support a gateway or proxy in front so we can keep our existing auth and rate-limiting?
[01:33] Jordan Lee: Yes — many customers use a gateway pattern. You can run a lightweight proxy that does auth, token transformation and request shaping. Redwood also supports routing rules so requests can be sent to hosted/dedicated/private per route.
[01:50] Maya Patel: How about SDKs — we use LangChain and LlamaIndex heavily. Are there examples?
[01:56] Priya Shah: We have SDKs for Python/Node and official connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex. I'll share a code snippet after the call. For LangChain, we surface streaming and function-calling where supported.
[02:08] Ethan Brooks: Any quirks with LlamaIndex? We embed using their document loader and then call embeddings.
[02:13] Priya Shah: Embeddings are first-class — batching, async calls, and caching. With LlamaIndex you'll typically use our embedding API key via the SDK; we also have sample prompt templates.
[02:22] Maya Patel: Observability — we need token-level cost, per-route latency, and traces that tie back to our request IDs.
[02:29] Priya Shah: Redwood Console provides per-route dashboards, token cost breakdowns and tracing hooks. You can pass your request_id header; traces will show in the console and we export logs to your S3 or SIEM — depends on plan.
[02:42] Linh Tran: Do you expose hooks for Prometheus or OpenTelemetry?
[02:46] Priya Shah: We export traces via OTLP and metrics via Prometheus endpoints that you can scrape from our private deployment or push via exporters. Hosted plans have log/webhook exports.
[02:58] Ethan Brooks: For rate limits, do you support token-based quotas vs request-count? We have bursty short requests that are token-light but qps-sensitive.
[03:07] Jordan Lee: We have both. Quotas can be on tokens and requests; you can configure route-level rate limits and global account quotas. For bursty qps, you can set higher ephemeral burst limits on a per-route basis and tie to billing.
[03:21] Maya Patel: Data residency — certain PII flows must stay in EU. Is Private deployment required or do you have region pinning on hosted?
[03:30] Priya Shah: Hosted supports region pinning to our EU region and also supports data residency controls, but for strict regulatory requirements we recommend Private (VPC) with customer-managed networking and KMS integration.
[03:42] Maya Patel: KMS — can we bring our own key?
[03:45] Priya Shah: Yes, both Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. Hosted can support limited BYOK for enterprise contracts.
[03:55] Ethan Brooks: Latency SLOs — 95th p95 for us needs to be under 300ms for short completions. Can Redwood guarantee that on hosted?
[04:05] Jordan Lee: Hosted has best-effort p95 that varies by model and region. Dedicated gives you SLA-backed latency targets because capacity is reserved. For strict SLOs, Dedicated or Private is recommended.
[04:18] Maya Patel: Pricing — we need a simple TCO comparison for tokens and reserved cost.
[04:23] Jordan Lee: I'll send a hosted vs dedicated pricing sheet with an example TCO model based on your throughput. We'll include quantization and batching recommendations that often cut costs 20-40%.
[04:35] Linh Tran: Regarding gateways — we run Kong/Envoy today. Any tips to avoid double rate-limiting or tokenization mismatches?
[04:43] Priya Shah: Common pattern is to keep your edge proxy for auth/rate-limits and send a normalized request to Redwood. Use a shared header for original client_id for attribution. For tokenization mismatches, we recommend server-side token counting via our SDK before sending large batches.
[04:58] Ethan Brooks: For embeddings batch jobs at night — can you schedule jobs to use lower-cost quantized endpoints?
[05:04] Priya Shah: Yes, we support model variants and routing rules by time of day. You can route batch embeddings to quantized models or lower-cost capacity pools automatically.
[05:14] Maya Patel: Any references for LangChain + Redwood patterns?
[05:17] Priya Shah: I'll share a repo link with examples — LangChain agent loops, LlamaIndex document loaders pointing to our embeddings, and a short notebook for async batching.
[05:26] Jordan Lee: Quick note on security docs — we have SOC2 and ISO summaries, SAML SSO guides, and KMS integration docs. I'll attach the security pack.
[05:36] Maya Patel: Great. On sign-off process — who would need to be involved? Our procurement and legal will look at data residency and indemnities, and engineering will validate benchmarks.
[05:45] Jordan Lee: Typical flow: tech deep-dive + benchmark, procurement review contract terms, then PoC or pilot. For Dedicated/Private we also do a security questionnaire.
[05:55] Linh Tran: Timeline — we hope to decide within 6 weeks, budget cycle at end of quarter.
[06:00] Priya Shah: That's workable. We'll do a benchmark run and aim to return results within 10 business days after we get your sample traffic.
[06:08] Ethan Brooks: For the benchmark, what telemetry do you need?
[06:11] Priya Shah: Sample prompt sets, qps distribution, desired models, and any input/output size constraints. Ideally a replayable subset.
[06:20] Maya Patel: We'll gather that. A couple of detailed questions: 1) If we use a proxy, will function-calling and streaming still work? 2) Any issues with LlamaIndex chunking causing extra tokens billed?
[06:34] Priya Shah: 1) Streaming and function-calling work through proxies if you proxy websockets or allow chunked transfer encoding. 2) Chunking is something we see — better to dedupe on the client or use cache keys. We'll show typical LlamaIndex patterns that reduce token churn.
[06:52] Jordan Lee: I want to recap next steps: Priya will share SDK + LangChain/LlamaIndex examples and a repo link; I'll send pricing and security pack; Synergy to share sample traffic for benchmarking; schedule a technical deep-dive the week of 6/22.
[07:05] Maya Patel: That sounds right. Any blockers from your side?
[07:09] Priya Shah: Nothing blocking — one ask: if you have compliance questions please list them so we address in the security pack.
[07:15] Ethan Brooks: Will do. Also can you include a short runbook for failover from dedicated to hosted? We want to know fallback behavior if capacity exhausted.
[07:23] Jordan Lee: Absolutely — we'll include routing/fallback docs and example configs.
[07:29] Linh Tran: One more — observability export formats and retention for logs. We need 1 year retention for audit logs.
[07:36] Priya Shah: Private + Dedicated can support 1 year retention with the enterprise add-on; hosted has configurable retention windows. We'll add retention details to the security pack.
[07:46] Maya Patel: Great, thanks Jordan and Priya.
[07:49] Jordan Lee: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the materials by Friday.
[07:53] (recording ends, omitted final small talk)
